title: Knowledge check: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “How CSRF works” under lesson 195, “Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for security and privacy.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)”?
options: Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)” in a real application?
options: Enforce authorization and data scope on the server for every protected operation.
Hide the link in HTML and trust that users cannot call the URL directly.
Treat a login session as proof of permission to access every object.
Use a client-submitted user ID as the sole authorization check.
questions.answer_key: Enforce authorization and data scope on the server for every protected operation.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of Security and Privacy. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.
